sources.title: Optimizing performance through intrinsic motivation and attention for learning: The OPTIMAL theory of motor learning
Additive benefits of autonomy support and enhanced expectancies for motor learning
sources.authors: Wulf G, Chiviacowsky S, Cardozo PL.

sources.title: Optimizing motivation and attention for motor performance and learning
Additive benefits of external focus and enhanced performance expectancy for motor learning
sources.authors: Pascua LA, Wulf G, Lewthwaite R.

findings.finding: Expectancy effects may be rooted in dopamine responses to anticipated positive experiences during practice.
findings.quote: We describe a plausible mechanism for expectancy effects rooted in responses of dopamine to the anticipation of positive experience and temporally associated with skill practice.

findings.finding: Providing autonomy support and enhanced expectancies independently and jointly benefit motor skill learning.
findings.quote: Thus, supporting learners' need for autonomy by given them a small choice--even though it was not directly related to task performance--and enhancing their performance expectancies appeared to independently influence learning.

findings.finding: The combination of autonomy support and enhanced expectancies yields the greatest accuracy during retention and transfer tests.
findings.quote: Autonomy support and enhanced expectancies had additive advantages for learning, with both main effects being significant for retention and transfer. On both tests, the AS/EE group showed the greatest throwing accuracy.

findings.finding: Positive affect is heightened by enhanced expectancies and predicts better transfer performance.
findings.quote: Positive affect was heightened in the enhanced expectancy and enhanced expectancy groups after practice and predicted transfer performance.

principle: Enhanced performance expectancies and autonomy support both improve motor learning and performance, and their benefits can be additive when combined.
for_the_teacher: Provide learners with small choices during practice, such as selecting the color of a practice tool, to support their autonomy.
Give positive social-comparative feedback to enhance learners' performance expectancies.
Combine autonomy support and enhanced expectancies in lessons to maximize learning and retention accuracy.
